title: Dictionaries and sets

outcomes.can: Build and update counts in a Dictionary.
Read a key that may be missing without stopping the program.
Collect unique values with a HashSet.

intro: A list finds items by position. A Dictionary finds a value by its key, and a HashSet keeps each value only once. This module covers both, including what happens when a key is missing.

steps.title: Find a value by its key
steps.text: A Dictionary<string, int> stores pairs: a string key and an int value for it. open["Ana"] = 2; stores 2 under the key "Ana", adding the key if it is new and replacing the value if it exists. open["Ana"] reads the value. Reading a key that is not there stops the program with a KeyNotFoundException. To be safe, ask first with ContainsKey, or use TryGetValue. open.TryGetValue("Cy", out int found) returns true and puts the value in found when the key exists, and returns false when it does not. The word out marks a variable that the method fills in. Count is the number of keys.

steps.title: Update a count
steps.text: Follow the value stored under "Ana". Predict the first two lines of output.

steps.title: Follow the dictionary
steps.text: Ana starts at 2. The fourth line reads 2, adds 1 and stores 3 back under the same key, so Ana is 3 and there are still only two keys. "Cy" was never added. ContainsKey returns False, and TryGetValue returns false, so the else block prints "no entry". Reading open["Cy"] directly would have stopped the program.

steps.title: Keep each value once
steps.text: A HashSet<string> holds values with no repeats. Add returns true when the value was new and false when the set already had it. Contains tests for a value, and Count is the number of different values.

steps.title: Add a repeat
steps.text: "Ana" is added to the set twice. Predict the last two lines of output.

steps.title: Follow the set
steps.text: The first two Add calls return true, and their results are not used. The third adds "Ana" again. The set already has it, so Add returns False and the set does not grow. Count is 2.

steps.title: Count tasks per owner
steps.text: The starter records every owner but never counts above 1. Repair the update.

steps.title: Look up a task's minutes
steps.text: Work from the prompt. The case box supplies a dictionary to read from.

questions.prompt: What are the first two lines of output?

choices.feedback: The fourth line stores a new value for Ana: the old 2 plus 1.
Ana is updated to 3. Storing under an existing key replaces its value and adds no key.
Storing under a key that exists replaces the value. The dictionary still has two keys.

questions.prompt: What are the last two lines of output?

choices.feedback: The set already had Ana, so Add returns False and the count stays at 2.
A set keeps each value once. Adding Ana again changes nothing.
Add returned False because nothing was added, so the count is still 2.

review.evidence: Open a fresh starter on a later visit, with the earlier answer closed. A first unaided pass on every case is later evidence of the skill. A hinted pass stays recorded as assisted.

drillGap: These drills practise one dictionary call each. They do not check repeated keys, missing keys and stored zeros together.
